text:
marta: starting a small canary for rwdv6-int4 on /api/generate — 2% traffic, timeframe 1h. shadow comparisons + smoke eval ran earlier, dropping quick notes here.

oliver: good. any immediate red flags from the smoke eval?

marta: smoke summary (short):
```
- latency: +9ms p95 vs rwdv5 (baseline)
- token loss (avg): +0.02
- prompt-set-A exact-match: -0.4%
- safety hallucination slice: +0.8% (small n)
- throughput unchanged
```

marta: also saw a few formatting regressions on long-code prompts — examples in the dashboard: https://console.redwood/boards/rollouts/1719876543

julie: +1 to watch hallucination delta closely. do we have an automatic fallback config for this route?

kevin: current policy for /api/generate:
- auto-fallback if hallucination_rate_delta > 0.5pp OR
- avg_output_quality_score drop > 1.0 (on normalized scale) OR
- latency p95 increase > 20ms
Fallback is immediate to rwdv5 and an incident ticket is created.

marta: ok. hallucination delta is 0.8% in smoke (above 0.5pp) but small sample. curious if shadow traffic confirms. can we hold traffic and run 30m shadow?

oliver: +1 to shadow for 30m. if shadow confirms >0.6pp we should flip the auto-fallback.

ci-bot: deploy-bot started canary for rwdv6-int4 on 2% -> shard-17 at 1719876600. Logs available: https://ci.redwood/runs/7801

marta: running a quick targeted eval set (safety-focused + longform code). will post results in ~25m.

[25m later]

marta: shadow 30m results: hallucination delta consolidated to +0.65pp on the safety slice, long-code formatting regressions persistent on 3/50 samples. latency p95 holds at +10ms.

julie: that crosses the 0.5pp threshold but not huge. question: do we treat safety slice differently (lower tolerance)?

kevin: we do. safety_slice_tolerance = 0.25pp for auto-fallback. any >0.25pp triggers immediate rollback for safety-sensitive routes. /api/generate is marked safety-sensitive.

oliver: oh — that means we're already over the safety threshold. recommend immediate flip to rwdv5 and run postmortem on quantization artifacts.

marta: initiating rollback now.

ci-bot: rollback triggered by marta at 1719876655. Canary traffic reverted to rwdv5. Incident created: INC-2026-428.

marta: filing quick notes: possible causes = quantization rounding for attention scores at long contexts, kv-cache indexing edge-case, and decoder tokenization differences. next steps:
- small repro for long-code formatting (collect examples)
- run int8 vs int4 layer-wise ablation for attention layers
- run deterministic seed comparisons to isolate tokenizer mismatch
- consider temporary hold on rwdv6-int4 for safety-sensitive routes until fix

oliver: sound plan. can we add an explicit gate to block auto-promote of int4 variants on safety routes until they pass a dedicated safety-eval (n>500)?

kevin: sure — I'll update rollout-config: add key `safety_min_eval_n=500` and `safety_auto_fallback_threshold=0.25` for future canaries.

julie: thanks all. nice quick shadow + rollback — kept customer-facing impact minimal. :thumbsup:

marta: will post follow-up with repro logs and a proposed ablation matrix.
